Olivia (People Ops): Thanks everyone for the All‑Hands today — leaving this thread open for follow-ups on hybrid/office ops, travel, and offsite logistics. Ask here and I'll summarize action items. :wave:

Mason (Eng): Quick one — if I need to go to SF for a customer meeting for 2 days, what approvals do I need?

Olivia (People Ops): Short answer: manager ok + expense pre-approval for trips > $1k. Please use the TravelForm: <https://intranet/redwood/travel|TravelForm> and tag your manager. People Ops will auto-approve routine trips. :white_check_mark:

Maya (Office Ops): Also note: if you're booking >48hrs in advance and need a desk in SF hub, put the booking in the Hub calendar. We hold 10 desks for intercity travel — first come, first served.

Mason (Eng): Cool — for offsites (team retreat) — what's the budget per person and approval flow?

Olivia (People Ops): For team offsites: default company contribution is $600/person for domestic, $1,200/person international. Submit an Offsite Request form (link pinned in #people-ops) and include rough itinerary + spend estimate. Exec sign-off required for >$10k total.

Sam (Dir, Eng): Can teams top-up from headcount budgets? Example: we'd like to add an extra day on the offsite.

Olivia (People Ops): Yes — teams can cover top-ups via their project budget. Put that in the Offsite Request and mark "team top-up". Finance will reconcile.

Ken (CTO): For roadmapping clarity — people traveling for roadmap reviews should prefer scheduled review weeks (see roadmap calendar). If travel conflicts with major rollout days, talk to your PM/manager first.

Mason (Eng): Any guidance on international visa/travel paperwork?

Maya (Office Ops): For international travel, start 6+ weeks out. Office Ops can help with invitation letters. For visas requiring company sponsorship, ping me @Maya and provide passport details (secure channel will be used).

Olivia (People Ops): Health & safety: company covers required vaccines and emergency medical evacuation insurance for approved international travel. Add a note in the TravelForm if you need coverage.

Mason (Eng): What's the policy on remote work during travel? If I'm in SF for customer meetings, can I still be remote the rest of the week?

Olivia (People Ops): You can follow your team's hybrid schedule. If you're on the road, let your manager know; we ask that you mark status in Slack and update calendar blocks. No special approval needed for working remotely while traveling, unless it impacts cross-team availability.

Sam (Dir, Eng): Offsite venue accessibility question — any checklist we should run before booking?

Maya (Office Ops): Yes — accessibility, AV capabilities, breakout rooms, Wi‑Fi SLA, and catering options. I can share a short venue checklist template.

Mason (Eng): Can we expense coworking days when visiting another city?

Olivia (People Ops): Yes — coworking/day passes are expensable under "travel/stay" up to a reasonable monthly cap. Put a short justification in the expense.

Ken (CTO): One more ops note: if you're reserving long-term desks in a satellite hub, reach out to Office Ops for allocation — we prefer centralized coordination to avoid hotspots.
